summary: Brunswick Executive Airport (NHZ/KBXM) occupies the site of the former Naval Air Station Brunswick, a U.S. Navy installation that operated from 1952 until its closure in 2011. The facility was redeveloped as a civilian airport and business park on the scenic midcoast Maine peninsula along the Androscoggin River. Its unusually long runways—remnants of its military past—make it one of the largest general aviation airfields in Maine and capable of handling larger business jets than most regional airports.
faqs:
Q: What is the history of Brunswick Executive Airport?
A: The airport is located on the former Naval Air Station Brunswick, which served as a home base for P-3 Orion maritime patrol squadrons until it was closed in 2011 under the BRAC process. The site was transferred to the Midcoast Regional Redevelopment Authority and reopened as a civilian airport.

Q: How large is Brunswick Executive Airport?
A: The airfield features one of the longest runways in the state of Maine, originally built to accommodate naval aircraft. The site spans several thousand acres of developable land surrounding the runway complex.

Q: What types of aircraft use the airport?
A: It primarily serves general aviation traffic, corporate jets, and occasional military training operations. The long runway allows it to accommodate larger business jets and cargo aircraft that cannot use smaller regional airports.

Q: Are there commercial airline services at KBXM?
A: No, Brunswick Executive is not served by scheduled commercial airlines. Travelers typically use Portland International Jetport, located about 30 miles southwest, for commercial flights.
